event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: WEC’s 2024 Form 10-K frames COVID-19 (and future pandemics) chiefly as an ongoing, enterprise-wide hazard rather than a past, fully-realised shock.  The risk language is forward-looking and largely qualitative, emphasising potential—not yet fully quantified—financial, operational and strategic impacts: lost revenue, higher bad-debt, capital-market access problems, supply-chain inflation, project delays, and workforce disruptions.  The company also concedes substantial uncertainty around magnitude and duration, signalling limited visibility into residual effects four years after the World Health Organization declaration.  Under the Time Decay Principle, COVID-19 sits at the edge of the 0-3-year “recent” band and in the early stage of the 4-10-year “medium-term” window; consequently, individual evidence snippets merit moderate scores (4-6) unless tempered by mitigating language such as acknowledgements of uncertainty or management efforts.  No sentence provides hard dollar figures or cites realised losses, so scores do not reach the highest tier.  Overall, the disclosure points to a material but still largely contingent risk that could hinder WEC’s strategy execution and financial performance if another severe wave or comparable public-health crisis emerges.

evidence_list.snippet: Public health crises, including epidemics and pandemics, could adversely affect our business functions, financial condition, liquidity, and results of operations.

components.reason: Explicitly links pandemics to broad negative impacts across multiple financial dimensions (‘business functions, financial condition, liquidity, and results of operations’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic but clear statement of enterprise-wide harm yields a moderate score within the 4-6 band appropriate for a medium-term risk.

evidence_list.snippet: Public health crises, including epidemics and pandemics, and any related government responses may adversely impact the economy and financial markets and could have a variety of adverse impacts on us, including a decrease in revenues; increased bad debt expense; increases in past due accounts receivable balances; and access to the capital markets at unreasonable terms or rates.

components.reason: Lists several concrete financial stress channels (revenue fall-off, bad-debt spike, liquidity squeeze).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Greater specificity on financial mechanics elevates severity, but lack of quantification keeps the score at the high end of the medium range.

evidence_list.snippet: Public health crises, including epidemics and pandemics, and any related government responses could also impair our ability to develop, construct, and operate facilities.

components.reason: Highlights direct operational threat to capital projects and existing assets.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Operational impairment risk is material but unquantified, resulting in a mid-level score.

evidence_list.snippet: Risks include extended disruptions to supply chains and inflation, resulting in increased costs for labor, materials, and services, which could adversely impact our ability to implement our corporate strategy.

components.reason: Connects pandemic-related supply-chain and inflation pressures to higher input costs.
Links cost pressures to execution of corporate strategy, indicating strategic risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific identification of supply-chain and cost inflation impacts justifies a solid mid-range score.

evidence_list.snippet: We may also be adversely impacted by labor disruptions and productivity as a result of infections, employee attrition, and a reduced ability to replace departing employees as a result of employees who leave or forego employment to avoid any required precautionary measures.

components.reason: Details human-capital and productivity risks stemming from infections and precautionary measures.
Forward-looking ‘may’ language keeps it within potential, not realised, risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Workforce disruption is a concrete operational threat; absence of metrics keeps the score moderate.

evidence_list.snippet: Despite our efforts to manage the impacts of public health crises, including epidemics and pandemics, that may occur in the future, the extent to which they may affect us depends on factors beyond our knowledge or control. As a result, we are unable to determine the potential impact any such public health crises, including epidemics and pandemics, may have on our business plans and operations, liquidity, financial condition, and results of operations.

components.reason: Acknowledges pandemic risk remains but stresses uncertainty and management’s inability to quantify impact.
Mitigating language (‘unable to determine’, ‘beyond our control’) reduces perceived immediacy.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Uncertainty disclaimer offsets generic risk mention, yielding a negligible net severity score.
